subject: Urgent: Project Atlas SLA shortfall and cross-org coordination
messages:
From: Elena Torres <elena@atlashealth.com>
To: aditya_rao@redwood.com
Cc: support@atlashealth.com, legal@atlashealth.com
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Unacceptable latency spikes impacting production (Atlas)

Hi Aditya —

We started seeing sustained 95th percentile latency > 3s and a sharp increase in 5xx error rate this morning (around 08:50 PDT). This is affecting our triage pipeline and causing retries in downstream services. We have already throttled some requests client-side but the business impact is material for our care routing.

Can you confirm:
- Whether this is a busy-hour pattern or a systemic regression?
- If there is a rollback or mitigation plan you can enact immediately?
- An ETA for a fix and what data you need from our side?

Attached: small sample of errors and request ids. We need an executive-level status and clear next steps; our CTO is asking for an update in 30 minutes.

Thanks,
Elena Torres
VP, Engineering — Atlas Health

Attachments:
- atlas-error-log-20270511.txt (text/plain, 42KB)
From: aditya_rao@redwood.com
To: Elena Torres <elena@atlashealth.com>, support@atlashealth.com
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, evelyn_hart@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 09:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Unacceptable latency spikes impacting production (Atlas)

Elena —

Thanks for the quick heads-up and for the logs. I’m escalating immediately. Preliminary notes from my team: we’re seeing a sudden increase in queue latency on the hosted route serving Atlas, correlated with a degraded KV cache hit rate after a partial model rollout at 08:40 PDT. Error traces point to transient memory pressure leading to redispatch retries.

Immediate actions (in progress):
- Rolling back the 08:40 model rollout to the last verified variant (started 09:20 PDT).
- Spinning an additional dedicated worker pool in us-west to offload traffic (started 09:22 PDT).
- Capturing full request tracing and token-level latency for the affected window.

I’m standing up a cross-org coordination thread and an exec readout. Lauren — can you join an ad-hoc bridge? Evelyn — please pull the SLA telemetry and recent canary metrics; Marcus, want infra on standby for any cluster-level intervention.

We’ll provide a short executive update in ~30 minutes and a customer-facing statement after we confirm stabilization.

Apologies for the disruption — we understand the impact and are prioritizing.

Regards,
Aditya Rao
Director, Customer Reliability — Redwood Inference

Referenced attachments: atlas-error-log-20270511.txt
From: aditya_rao@redwood.com
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, evelyn_hart@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Cc: Elena Torres <elena@atlashealth.com>, ops@cloudops.example
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 09:40:00 -07:00
Subject: [Internal] Incident sync: Atlas SLA shortfall — immediate actions and exec cadence

Team —

Summary (so far):
- Impact: Atlas saw a 95th pctl latency spike to ~3.6s and a 5xx surge from baseline 0.2% to ~2.8% between 08:48–09:10 PDT. Business impact: queued requests and retries in customer pipelines.
- Suspected cause: partial model variant rollout at 08:40 PDT reduced cache efficacy; increased memory churn and per-request redispatch.
- Short-term mitigations in flight: rollback of model variant (09:20), extra worker pool (09:22), throttling on noncritical routes for Atlas (09:30).

Immediate ask list:
1) Lauren: prepare a 5-slide exec snapshot for the C-suite (impact, root cause hypothesis, mitigations, customer comms, next steps). Need by 10:00 PDT.
2) Evelyn: pull token-level P95, error traces, and ingress QPS for the past 90 minutes; attach dashboard snapshot.
3) Marcus: be prepared to scale the GPU pool or perform node-level restarts if rollback does not staunch the error rate. Confirm availability of reserved capacity.
4) Monica (CS): draft a short customer-facing update we can send at stabilization; include acknowledgement, what we did, expected next steps, and an offer for a follow-up post-mortem.

Bridge: Zoom — join now (lauren will start and post link). We may add execs: Evelyn, please prepare a 10-minute tech brief for the CTO and CPO.

Logging/Artifacts: attaching a snapshot of the latency dashboard (latency-dashboard-20270511.png) and the small error sample Elena sent. Link to incident tracker: https://redwood.internal/ops/incident/ATL-2027-05-11

We need crisp, aligned messaging — no speculative causes in customer comms. I’ll own the external notify after we confirm the rollback results.

— Aditya
From: aditya_rao@redwood.com
To: Elena Torres <elena@atlashealth.com>, support@atlashealth.com
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, evelyn_hart@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 13:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Update: Atlas service stabilized — next steps and post-mortem plan

Elena —

Quick update following the rollback and scaling actions: service has returned to baseline (95th pctl ~0.8s, 5xx <0.4%) as of 12:46 PDT. Timeline:
- 08:40 PDT: model variant rollout (canary)
- 08:48–09:10 PDT: latency and error spike observed by Atlas
- 09:20 PDT: rollback initiated
- 09:22 PDT: extra worker pool spun up; throttles on noncritical routes applied
- 12:46 PDT: metrics back to baseline; ongoing monitoring

What we’ll do next:
- Post-mortem: we’ll produce a joint incident report within 72 hours with root cause analysis, impact quantification, and follow-up actions (config changes, improved canary gates).
- Immediate compensatory offer: we’re prepared to propose a one-time credit for the affected window; Monica will coordinate specifics.
- Prevention: tighter canary gating (token-level sample checks), KV cache warmup pre-rollout, and an automated rollback if memory-churn thresholds breach.

Please let us know if you need a separate readout for your CTO/ops team. We appreciate the quick coordination and will share the post-mortem draft for Atlas review.

Regards,
Aditya Rao
Director, Customer Reliability — Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: latency-dashboard-20270511.png
